"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3968: a 'g' + 'l' spelling detector inside words.

The component is negative when a word, spelled out of several pieces, has the letters g then
l across a piece boundary, with the l opening a piece that does not begin a word:
hypo|gly|caemia (the 'ly' piece), Asn-G|ly, Heig|l|in, Ultrag|lide, Tarsalg|li|eder,
sang|l|ante. It is strongest for rare or technical words and weak for common ones such as
Verg|leich. Weaker negative responses: a word-internal piece that itself contains gl
(hyper|gly|cemia), a word-initial piece beginning gl (' gly', ' glor', ' Glo', ' gluc'),
and continuation pieces after an earlier gl in the same word. Cyrillic г and л count as g
and l. The repeated middle-dot filler '··' gives a small positive value (it is rare).
Everything else is near zero.

The program tracks the word spelled so far (carry), restarts it at document starts and at
any piece with a leading space or no letters, and reads only the newest token.
"""

READS = ()

STRADDLE_L = -2.5     # word-internal piece starting with l, right after a piece ending in g
GL_INSIDE = -0.6      # word-internal piece containing gl
GL_WORD_START = -0.5  # word-initial piece containing gl
GL_EARLIER = -0.3     # continuation piece after an earlier gl in the same word
DOTS = 0.5            # the repeated middle-dot filler


def _fold(text):
    return text.lower().replace("г", "g").replace("л", "l")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = carry or ""
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    lead = cur[:1].isspace()
    if lead:
        word = ""
    value = 0.0
    if cur == "··":
        value = DOTS
    before = "gl" in _fold(word)
    after = "gl" in _fold(word + cur)
    inside = not lead and word != ""
    if after and not before:
        if not inside:
            value = GL_WORD_START
        elif _fold(cur).startswith("l"):
            value = STRADDLE_L
        else:
            value = GL_INSIDE
    elif after and before and inside:
        value = GL_EARLIER
    new_word = cur if lead else word + cur
    if not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in cur):
        new_word = ""
    return new_word, value

"""A small predictor for Latin fragments in Spanish/Portuguese-like text.

A decaying tally of grammatical words estimates the ongoing language. In that
context, tokens containing t give positive values. Otherwise, d-bearing
tokens and fragments ending in g give negative values. Length, whitespace,
and grammatical-word status adjust the size. Other tokens stay near zero.
The colon in a document-initial Title: field has a separate negative response.
"""
READS = ()

IBERIAN_WORDS = set("""
el la los las del y en que de por para un una con se su sus al es lo
como más pero este esta entre cuando todo porque hay muy también
o os as do da dos das não uma em com ao é são você eu um no na nos
nas mas mais foi está
""".split())
CONTRAST_WORDS = set("""
the and of to in is for that with are was on it this be at by from or
an not have has but we you they he she its can will would
le les des du et une dans est pas pour avec sur qui il elle au aux ce ne par
het een van voor dat zijn op aan niet om ook met dit als maar wordt
di che non per della gli sono delle dello
der die und ist zu den von mit ein eine auf dem nicht
""".split())


def fragment_response(token, word):
    short = len(word) <= 3
    if 't' in word:
        return 0.62 if short else 0.113
    if word.endswith('d'):
        return -1.713 if short else -0.507
    if 'd' in word:
        if token.startswith(' ') and word in IBERIAN_WORDS:
            return -0.085
        return -0.246 if token.startswith(' ') else -0.579
    if word.endswith('g'):
        return -0.525
    return 0.01


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    same_doc = carry is not None and carry[0] == doc
    score = carry[1] if same_doc else 0.0
    position = carry[2] + 1 if same_doc else 0
    previous = carry[3] if same_doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    score = 0.98 * score
    score += (word in IBERIAN_WORDS) - (word in CONTRAST_WORDS)
    language_gate = max(0.0, min(1.0, (score - 3) / 4))
    value = language_gate * fragment_response(token, word)
    if position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = -11.207
    return (doc, score, position, token), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 3969: a weak, mostly unpredictable signal.

Plain-terms summary of what this program predicts:
- Its activation is near zero almost everywhere; its large values are rare, and their sign
  is not predictable from simple features. So the program predicts small values only.
- Inside a word (a token with no leading space, letters only, not the first token of its
  document), the sign leans with the piece's last letter: pieces ending in t or u tend to be
  positive, pieces ending in d, g, b or h tend to be negative (e.g. the Spanish/Portuguese
  participle endings "ad", "id", "ido", "ida" lean negative, "ato", "ata" lean positive).
- A colon right after a "Title" header at the start of a document is strongly negative.
- The first token of a document has no left context and is set to 0.
"""

READS = ()

POS_LAST = set("tu")
NEG_LAST = set("dgbh")
SCALE = 0.01
TITLE_COLON = -6.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n = 0
    else:
        n = carry[1] + 1
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if n > 0 and not tok.startswith(" ") and tok.strip().isalpha():
        last = tok.strip()[-1].lower()
        if last in POS_LAST:
            value = SCALE
        elif last in NEG_LAST:
            value = -SCALE
    if n == 1 and tok == ":" and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() == "Title":
        value = TITLE_COLON
    return (doc, n), value

"""Import-target detector: fires on the package name in an import statement.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3970 is quiet almost everywhere (it fires on ~0.06% of
tokens). When it fires, it is on the word that names the package being imported, in source
code, just after the keyword that starts the import:

  Python  `from collections import ...`   the module after a line-initial `from`
          `from django.contrib.auth`      the next package segment (`.auth`)
          `from . import x`               the relative dot
  Rust    `use std::...`                  `std` (strongest), `crate`, `super`
  C#      `using System;`                 the namespace after `using`, and `.Collections`
  Java    `import java.util.List;`        the `.util` / `.io` after `import java`

Strength depends on how familiar the package is: well-known libraries and the Python
standard library (typing, datetime, os, numpy, django, ...) give large values, short or
unknown local names (`q`, `bump`, `slack`) and English words give almost nothing.

The program tracks the current line as tokens arrive (a literal "\\n" also counts as a line
break, since code often appears escaped inside JSON strings). A document counts as code once
it has a line that starts like an import, a #include, a package/using/use, a def or a class,
or once it begins a new document; prose "from the ..." lines are then ignored.
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

LEAD_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^\d+\t")  # line numbers in pasted file views: "   12\tfrom x"
NEWLINE = re.compile(r"\\n|\n")  # a real or escaped line break
CODE_START = re.compile(
    r"^(import \w|from \S+ import |#include|package |using \w|use \w+::|def |class |public |#!)"
)

# Well-known packages: the Python standard library and popular third-party libraries.
WELL_KNOWN = {
    "typing", "collections", "datetime", "io", "os", "sys", "json", "re", "math", "random",
    "time", "urllib", "pathlib", "tempfile", "functools", "itertools", "logging", "subprocess",
    "unittest", "abc", "enum", "string", "socket", "threading", "queue", "shutil", "glob",
    "pickle", "csv", "copy", "struct", "argparse", "contextlib", "operator", "statistics",
    "tkinter", "hashlib", "ast", "http", "email", "xml", "sqlite3", "uuid", "base64", "asyncio",
    "multiprocessing", "dataclasses", "inspect", "numpy", "pandas", "scipy", "sklearn",
    "matplotlib", "torch", "tensorflow", "keras", "requests", "bs4", "flask", "django", "PIL",
    "cv2", "tqdm", "yaml", "pytest", "sqlalchemy", "werkzeug", "boto3", "selenium", "nltk",
    "gensim", "click", "pygame", "rich", "transformers", "seaborn", "celery", "redis",
}

# English words that can follow a line-initial "from" in prose.
ENGLISH = {
    "the", "this", "that", "these", "those", "his", "her", "its", "our", "your", "their", "my",
    "and", "for", "one", "some", "any", "each", "all", "both", "which", "what", "there", "here",
    "not", "with", "without", "where", "when", "about", "into", "from", "such", "other", "more",
    "most", "many", "much", "also", "just", "only", "like", "been", "being", "have", "has", "had",
    "are", "was", "were", "will", "can", "may", "should", "would", "could",
}


def _head(line):
    """The current line's text before this token, without indentation or line number."""
    return LEAD_NUMBER.sub("", NEWLINE.split(line)[-1].strip()).strip()


def _predict(head, tok, code):
    t = tok.strip()
    # Python: the module named right after a line-initial `from`
    if head == "from":
        if code and re.match(r"^[a-z_]\w*$", t) and len(t) > 2 and t not in ENGLISH:
            return 6.5 if t in WELL_KNOWN else 1.5
        if code and t == ".":
            return 3.0  # from . import x
        return 0.0
    if re.match(r"^from [\w.]+$", head):
        if tok.startswith(" import"):
            return 1.5
        if re.match(r"^\.[a-z]\w*$", tok):  # from django.contrib -> .auth
            return 3.0 if head.split()[1].split(".")[0] in WELL_KNOWN else 1.2
        return 0.0
    # Java / C#: import java.util, using System.Collections
    m = re.match(r"^(import|using) (\w+)$", head)
    if m and tok.startswith("."):
        if m.group(2) in ("java", "javax"):
            return 2.5
        if m.group(1) == "using":
            return 2.0
        return 1.0 if re.match(r"^\.[a-z]\w*$", tok) else 0.0
    # Rust: use std::..., use crate::..., use super::...
    if head == "use":
        return {"std": 7.5, "crate": 2.5, "super": 1.4}.get(t, 0.0)
    if re.match(r"^use \w+$", head) and tok == "::":
        return 1.4
    # C#: using System;   C++: using namespace std;
    if head == "using" and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_]\w*$", t) and t != "namespace":
        return 1.2
    if head.endswith("namespace") and t == "std":
        return 3.0
    # Python: `with open(` opening a block
    if head == "with" and tok == " open":
        return 6.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    # carry: (text of the current line so far, whether this document looks like code)
    line, code = ("", True) if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    value = _predict(_head(line), tok, code)
    if "<|" in tok:  # a special token (end of document, chat marker) starts a new text
        line, code = "", True
    else:
        segments = NEWLINE.split(line + tok)
        for seg in segments[:-1]:
            if CODE_START.match(_head(seg)):
                code = True
        line = segments[-1][-200:]
    return (line, code), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 3971: a token-type detector.

What it does: it reads the current token and guesses how strongly this component
pushes the residual stream, using a few coarse token types learned from the data:

- The first token of every document (where the attention has nothing before it)
  is strongly negative.
- Tab-indented code keywords (\\tdef, \\tfor, \\tvar ...) are strongly positive.
- Fragments of a multi-byte character (the U+FFFD replacement character) are positive.
- Code and markup punctuation, especially closing brackets such as ')', ']', '){',
  '][', '><', are positive; plain punctuation is near zero.
- Non-Latin scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, ...) are slightly positive.
- Plain English words, digits and whitespace are near zero.

Why: most of the variance is per-token and the component is nearly a pure token
lookup (the current token explains most of it; the previous token adds little), so a
short rule over token types captures the broad sign pattern, not the fine detail.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.8


def guess(tok):
    s = tok.strip()
    if "�" in tok:
        return 0.4
    if not s:
        return 0.0
    if s.isascii() and s.isalpha():
        return 0.6 if tok.startswith("\t") else 0.0
    if s.isdigit():
        return 0.0
    if not any(c.isascii() and c.isalnum() for c in s):
        if any(not c.isascii() and c.isalpha() for c in s):
            return 0.12
        multi = sum(1 for c in s if not c.isalnum()) >= 2
        if any(c in ")]}>" for c in s):
            return 0.33 if multi else 0.1
        return 0.23 if multi else 0.0
    return 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, DOC_START
    return None, guess(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Program for p-82af68dd@100000/layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3975 (layer 1 MLP down-projection).

What the component does, in plain terms: it is a weak, sparse, signed feature. Most of
the time it is near zero. It has two regimes that this program captures:

1. The first token of a document or of a packed row. The model has no earlier context
   there, so the component sits at a fixed negative offset (about -0.14 on average).

2. A word-piece that continues a word, inside French or Romanian text. When the text
   just before it contains accented letters, a short Romance word ending such as
   "-a", "-ia", "-ra", "-ea", "-era", "-ura", "-ina" (the ending of many French
   past-tense verb forms and Romanian nouns) is, on average, mildly positive
   (about +0.19). Examples: "ajout|a", "répud|ia", "env|oya".

Everything else is predicted as 0. The scatter around these group means is large, so
this explains only a small share of the variance (about 1-2% on training rows). A
token-by-token lookup table gets about 20% out of sample, but it is a long list of
rare word pieces with no shared meaning, so it is not included here.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Short word endings seen as continuation pieces of French and Romanian verb forms and nouns.
ROMANCE_ENDINGS = {
    "a", "ia", "ra", "ua", "ta", "ea", "ura", "era", "ina", "isa", "ssa",
    "uta", "oya", "erva", "ara", "ira", "ca", "va", "tra", "ita", "icia",
    "ica", "ire", "ere", "ul", "ie", "are",
}  # fmt: skip

ACCENTED = "àâçéèêëîïôûùüÿœæăâîșțşţ"
START_VALUE = -0.14  # first token of a document or row
ENDING_VALUE = 0.19  # Romance ending inside a word, in accented text
WINDOW = 64  # tokens of text looked back at for accents


def _starts_word(text: str) -> bool:
    return text[:1].isspace() or not text.strip()[:1].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if t == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return carry, START_VALUE
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    # A continuation piece: no leading space, lowercase letters, and it follows a word piece.
    is_continuation = not _starts_word(cur) and cur.islower() and not _starts_word(prev)
    if not is_continuation or cur.strip() not in ROMANCE_ENDINGS:
        return carry, 0.0
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-WINDOW:])
    if any(ch in ACCENTED for ch in recent.lower()):
        return carry, ENDING_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Chat boundaries, with a few strong document-opening formatting cues.

Message ends give a large negative response.  It is weaker after tool markup
or little preceding context, and stronger after ASCII sentence punctuation.
Recent non-ASCII text slightly softens it.  Other chat/reasoning tags have
smaller signed responses.  An initial ``Title:`` header and empty ``//``
comment line are separate strong cues.  Ordinary lexical variation is omitted.
"""
import re

READS = ()

MARKUP = {
    '</tool_call>': -0.38,
    '</tool_response>': 0.14,
    '<tool_call>': -0.12,
    '<tool_response>': 0.095,
    '<think>': 0.12,
    '</think>': -0.22,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        position, previous, tail = 0, '', ''
    else:
        _, position, previous, tail = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = MARKUP.get(token, 0.0)

    if token == '<|im_end|>':
        short_context = (position + 1) ** -0.65
        if previous in ('</tool_call>', '</tool_response>'):
            value = -1.45 if previous == '</tool_call>' else -1.50
            value += 1.13 * short_context
        else:
            sentence_end = bool(re.search(r'[.!?][\s"\')]*$', previous))
            non_ascii = any(ord(c) > 127 for c in tail)
            value = -1.97 - 0.12 * sentence_end + 0.08 * non_ascii
            value += 0.99 * short_context
    elif token == '<|im_start|>':
        value = -0.077 if position == 0 else 0.18
    elif token == '<|endoftext|>' and position == 0:
        value = -0.47
    elif position == 0 and token == 'Title':
        value = -0.86
    elif position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = -4.34
    elif position == 0 and token == '//\n':
        value = -1.97

    return (doc, position + 1, token, (tail + token)[-60:]), value

"""Turn-end detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 3976 (p-82af68dd).

In plain terms: this component is silent almost everywhere. Its one strong job is at
the chat turn-end marker <|im_end|>, where it writes a clearly negative value into the
residual stream. That value is about -2.0 when the turn ends after ordinary text, and
about -1.4 when the turn ends right after a tool call or tool response. A few other
chat-template markers get small values. A rare outlier: the colon in a document that
opens with "Title:" (right after <|endoftext|>) gets about -4.3. Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

TURN_END = "<|im_end|>"
TOOL_CLOSE = ("</tool_call>", "</tool_response>")
# small typical values on other chat-template markers
MARKERS = {
    "</tool_call>": -0.38,
    "</think>": -0.22,
    "<|im_start|>": 0.15,
    "</tool_response>": 0.14,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    tok = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = toks[-3] if len(toks) > 2 else ""
    if tok == TURN_END:
        value = -1.4 if prev in TOOL_CLOSE else -2.0
    elif tok == ":" and prev == "Title" and prev2 == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = -4.34
    else:
        value = MARKERS.get(tok, 0.0)
    return carry, value

"""A short-list syntax signal.

Predict a negative pulse on 'and/or' immediately after a comma, strongest
when the preceding comma-separated item is short. Predict positive pulses
for argument-like name=value assignments: familiar API options are strongest,
especially in parentheses, with longer names stronger than single letters.
A small pulse can already
appear on a familiar option name after a comma. This is a shallow text heuristic,
not a Python parser; quotation marks do not change the parentheses counter.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()

# Conventional options for plotting, arrays, argument parsing, and text output.
OPTIONS = frozenset('''
    color label fill alpha linewidth linestyle
    axis index key reverse dtype
    help action dest metavar choices default description nargs type
    file flush indent end sep encoding
    text width height row column font
    min max start stop step size shape name data
    batch_size random_state split
'''.split())
ARGUMENT = re.compile(r'([,(])\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*$')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', -100, 0, 0)
    _, tail, comma, parens, pos = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0

    if token in (' and', ' or') and pos - comma == 1:
        item = tail.rstrip()[:-1].rsplit(',', 1)[-1].strip()
        value = -2.4 * math.exp(-(len(item) / 19.5) ** 2)

    if parens and pos - comma == 1 and token.strip() in OPTIONS:
        value = 1.3

    equals = token.lstrip()
    if equals.startswith('=') and not equals.startswith(('==', '=>')):
        match = ARGUMENT.search(tail)
        if match:
            name = match[2]
            if name in OPTIONS:
                value = 4.8 if parens else 3.4
            elif len(name) == 1:
                value = 0.2 if parens else 0.1
            elif len(name) == 2:
                value = 1.3 if parens else 0.1
            else:
                value = 2.8 if parens else 0.9
            if token.startswith(' '):
                value *= 0.75

    for char in token:
        if char == '(':
            parens += 1
        elif char == ')':
            parens = max(0, parens - 1)
    if token.rstrip().endswith(','):
        comma = pos
    tail = (tail + token)[-300:]
    return (doc, tail, comma, parens, pos + 1), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection unit 3977 of Qwen3-1.7B, as a text rule.

The unit mostly sits near zero. Its large values come from two patterns in code and
in lists, both read from the text so far:

1. Keyword arguments in a function call. The "=" right after a parameter name, inside
   the call's parentheses, fires positively: `indent=2`, `skiprows=1`, `color='k'`.
   It fires less when the keyword is the call's first argument (`f(key=`, about 1.2)
   than when earlier arguments come before it (`f(x, key=`, about 2.6).
   An "=" outside a call (assignments, loops, LaTeX, HTML attributes) stays at 0.

2. Lists of short items. The "and" / "or" that closes a list of three or more
   comma-separated items fires negatively, and more so the shorter the items are:
   about -2 when the last item is one or two tokens (`A, B, and C`), about -1 at
   four tokens, and near 0 at seven or more (a clause, `..., and it is ...`).

Everywhere else the program predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

NAME = re.compile(r"\.?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*")
NOT_A_CALL = {"if", "elif", "while", "for", "and", "or", "not", "in", "return", "with",
              "assert", "lambda", "else"}
KW_FIRST = 1.2
KW_LATER = 2.6
LIST_SCALE = 0.3
SHORT_ITEM = 8


def _is_name(token):
    return bool(NAME.fullmatch(token)) and token.lstrip(".") not in NOT_A_CALL


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = tok.strip()
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        # open brackets as (is_call, arguments so far); the current list's comma count
        # and the length of its last item; the previous token
        brackets, commas, item, since, prev = (), 0, 0, 0, ""
    else:
        brackets, commas, item, since, prev = carry

    value = 0.0
    if s in ("and", "or") and prev == "," and commas >= 2:
        value = -LIST_SCALE * max(0, SHORT_ITEM - item)
    elif tok.startswith("=") and not tok.startswith("==") and brackets and brackets[-1][0]:
        if _is_name(prev):
            value = KW_LATER if brackets[-1][1] > 0 else KW_FIRST

    # update the state with this token
    for _ in range(tok.count("(")):
        brackets = brackets + ((_is_name(prev), 0),)
    for _ in range(tok.count(")")):
        brackets = brackets[:-1]
    if brackets and "," in tok:
        brackets = brackets[:-1] + ((brackets[-1][0], brackets[-1][1] + tok.count(",")),)
    if "\n" in tok:
        commas, item, since = 0, 0, 0
    elif "," in tok:
        commas, item, since = commas + 1, since, 0
    else:
        since += 1
    return (brackets, commas, item, since, s), value

"""Punctuation after numeric labels, list letters, and name initials.

A period or closing parenthesis is strong after a short label at a line's
start; tabs after printed source-code line numbers also receive a positive
estimate. The preceding line break, sentence ending, and open parentheses
help distinguish enumeration from ordinary prose or bracketed expressions.
Document-initial numbers are strongest. Other tokens receive zero.

import re

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0, 0, 0, '', '', False)
    _, line, position, dots, tabs, previous, boundary, was_number = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    number = re.search(r'([0-9]+)$', line)
    letter = re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z])([A-Za-z])$', line)
    number_dot = re.search(r'([0-9]+)\.$', line)
    label = number or letter or number_dot
    value = 0.0
    if label:
        before = line[:label.start()]
        start = not before.strip(' \t*#(["\'')
        fresh = before == '' and position == len(line)
        early = position <= 4
        one = label[1] == '1'
        spaced = bool(before) and before[-1].isspace()
        after_dot = before.endswith('.')
        after_letter = bool(before) and before[-1].isalpha()
        unmatched = before.count('(') > before.count(')')
        inline_colon = before.rstrip().endswith((':', '：'))
        gap = boundary if number else previous
        clean = gap.strip()
        blank = gap.count('\n') >= 2
        single = gap.count('\n') == 1
        sentence = clean.endswith(('.', '。'))
        colon = clean.endswith((':', '：'))
        space_gap = gap.isspace()
        newline = '\n' in token
        upper = token[1:2].isupper()
        lower = token[1:2].islower()
        if number:
            if token == '.':
                value = (-0.14 + 0.94*start + 0.63*one + 0.22*after_letter
                         + 0.74*blank + 0.58*single - 0.46*(sentence and blank)
                         + 0.29*colon + 0.25*space_gap)
                value /= 1 + position/256
                if fresh:
                    value = 6.34 if one else 5.1 - 0.11*int(number[1][-1])
            elif token.startswith('.'):
                value = (0.44 + 2.4*start + 0.53*spaced - 0.32*after_dot
                         - 0.38*after_letter - 0.5*newline + 0.55*upper
                         - 0.34*lower + 0.52*blank + 0.84*single
                         - 0.88*(sentence and blank) + 2.8*fresh)
            elif token.startswith(')'):
                value = (0.46 + 0.55*start + 0.14*one + 0.51*spaced
                         + 1.89*blank + 3.55*single - 1.94*sentence
                         + 0.65*inline_colon - 0.56*unmatched
                         + 1.96*after_dot - 0.57*colon - 0.41*space_gap
                         + 0.64*early + 0.4*fresh)
            elif token.startswith('\t'):
                value = (1.1 + 0.86*one + 0.23*(len(number[1]) > 1)
                         - 0.89*(len(number[1]) >= 3) - 1.25*newline
                         + 0.3*spaced + 0.18*space_gap)
                value /= 1 + tabs/16
            elif token.startswith((']', '}')):
                value = (0.05 + 0.24*start)/(1 + dots/16 + position/64)
        elif letter:
            if token == '.':
                value = (0.18 + 0.77*start - 0.13*letter[1].isupper()
                         - 0.11*after_dot - 0.19*after_letter
                         + 0.52*inline_colon - 0.24*fresh)
            elif token.startswith(')'):
                value = (0.59 + start - 0.62*unmatched + 0.59*upper
                         - 0.38*lower - 0.84*fresh)
            elif token.startswith('.'):
                value = (0.28 + 0.23*start - 0.28*after_dot
                         - 0.18*after_letter - 0.28*lower)/(1 + dots/16)
        elif number_dot and token.isspace():
            if '\t' in token:
                value = 2.27 + 2.27*start + 1.17*one
            else:
                value = 0.27 + 0.6*start - 0.36*newline + 0.1*one
                value += 0.39*after_dot - 0.11*unmatched
    if token.isascii() and token.isdigit():
        if not was_number:
            boundary = previous
        was_number = True
    else:
        was_number = False
    line = (line + token).rsplit('\n', 1)[-1][-160:]
    dots += token.startswith('.')
    tabs += token.startswith('\t')
    return (doc, line, position + 1, dots, tabs, token, boundary, was_number), float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3980.

What it does: this component is silent except at the first two tokens of a
document (positions reset at each new document, as in the model).

* First token of a document: a small negative value, about -0.27 on average
  (individual first tokens range from about -2.7 to +1.9; the average is used).
* Second token of a document: usually ~0, but a few two-token openings give
  large values: "Title:" -> -7.9, "1" "2" -> +6.7, "Posted on" -> +4.9,
  "{" "[" -> +3.9.
* Everywhere else: 0.

Because activations at the second token depend only on the first two tokens,
these are exact for the listed openings.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_MEAN = -0.27

# (first token, second token) at the start of a document -> activation
OPENING_BIGRAMS = {
    ("Title", ":"): -7.93,
    ("1", "2"): 6.74,
    ("Posted", " on"): 4.87,
    ("{", "["): 3.94,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        index, previous = 0, None
    else:
        index, previous = carry[0] + 1, carry[1]
    if index == 0:
        value = DOC_START_MEAN
    elif index == 1:
        value = OPENING_BIGRAMS.get((previous, token), 0.0)
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (index, token), value

"""Approximate an m-sensitive token feature, especially Greek mu in prose.

Recent Greek versus Latin letter counts approximate the distinction between
Greek prose and a mu used as a unit or variable. A following Greek letter gets a smaller continuation.
There are weaker m-onset terms in other scripts and a separate document-start
rule. These are coarse classes, not a lookup of individual token responses.
"""
import unicodedata as ud
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
from pypinyin import lazy_pinyin

READS = ()
M_KANA = frozenset('まみむめもマミムメモ')
GREEK_VOWELS = frozenset('αεηιουωΑΕΗΙΟΥΩ')


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def token_features(text):
    word = text.strip().lstrip('._/\\-\'"([{')
    first = word[:1]
    name = ud.name(first, '') if first else ''
    latin_m = first.lower() == 'm'
    cyrillic_m = first.lower() == 'м'
    han = 'CJK UNIFIED' in name or 'CJK COMPATIBILITY' in name
    han_m = han and lazy_pinyin(first)[0].startswith('m')
    onset_m = (latin_m or cyrillic_m or han_m or first in M_KANA
               or first in ('μ', 'Μ'))
    value = 0.001
    if latin_m:
        frequency = max(2.0, zipf_frequency(word, 'en'))
        value += 0.026 + 0.032 * (frequency - 5.0)
        value -= 0.042 * first.isupper()
        value += 0.079 * (len(word) == 1)
        if word.lower() == 'my':  # English first-person possessive
            value -= 0.238
    if cyrillic_m and len(word) > 1:
        value -= 0.085
    value += 0.053 * han_m
    value += 0.070 * any(c in M_KANA for c in word)
    value += 0.016 * ('GREEK' in name)
    greek = sum('GREEK' in ud.name(c, '') for c in text)
    latin = sum('LATIN' in ud.name(c, '') for c in text)
    mu = text.strip() in ('μ', 'Μ')
    vowel = ud.normalize('NFD', text.strip())[:1] in GREEK_VOWELS
    return word, onset_m, value, greek, latin, mu, vowel


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    greek_score, latin_score, after_mu = (0.0, 0.0, False) if start else carry[1:]
    word, onset_m, value, greek, latin, mu, vowel = token_features(
        prefix.token_strings[-1])
    greek_text = greek_score > 1.5 and greek_score > 2 * latin_score
    if start:
        if onset_m:
            value = 0.77
        elif word[:1].isalpha() and 'm' in word.lower():
            value = 0.10
        elif word[:1].isdigit():
            value = -0.16
        else:
            value = -0.23
    else:
        if mu:
            value += 1.788 * greek_text - 0.051
        if after_mu and greek:
            value += 0.884 if vowel else 0.290
    carry = (doc, 0.8 * greek_score + greek,
             0.8 * latin_score + latin, mu and greek_text)
    return carry, float(value)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3982: a Greek "mu" detector with two small side rules.

Main effect: the Greek letter mu (μ, µ, Μ) written inside Greek text fires strongly
positive (about 1.5). So does a Greek vowel that directly follows a mu, as in the
"mu-a", "mu-e" syllables of Greek words (about 1.2). A mu used as a unit or symbol
outside Greek text (µg, µl, µM) is slightly negative.

Side rules: the first token of each document or packed row is slightly negative
(about -0.19, the mean there), and the English word " my" is slightly negative.

Everything else is 0. Greek context means a Greek letter appears in the last five tokens.
"""

READS = ()
MU = set("μµΜ")
VOWELS = set("αεηιοωυάέήίόύώ")


def is_greek(ch):
    return "Ͱ" <= ch <= "Ͽ" or "ἀ" <= ch <= "῿"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, -0.19
    x = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-6:-1])
    greek_context = any(is_greek(ch) for ch in recent)
    if x in MU:
        return None, 1.5 if greek_context else -0.25
    if x and x[0] in VOWELS and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() in MU and greek_context:
        return None, 1.2
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] == " my":
        return None, -0.19
    return None, 0.0

"""Respond to Slavic stv/stw spellings, especially Russian -ств- endings.

The response is largest when a short token exposes the consonant cluster,
smaller when it is buried in a longer token, and persists into one inflectional
fragment.  Related sv spellings get a weaker response. Latin tv/tw crossings
are trusted mainly in recent Slavic-looking text. The separate Russian
preposition 'в' is mildly negative. These are spelling rules, not a dictionary
of individual words; they miss lexical and other contextual variation.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache

READS = ()
_TRANSLATE = str.maketrans({'с':'s','т':'t','в':'v',
                          'С':'S','Т':'T','В':'V'})

def normalize(text):
    text = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text.translate(_TRANSLATE))
    plain = ''.join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    return plain.lower().replace('w', 'v')

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(token):
    runs = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', token)
    lead = normalize(runs[0]) if runs and token[0].isalpha() else ''
    tail = normalize(runs[-1]) if runs and token[-1].isalpha() else ''
    cyrillic = any('\u0400' <= c <= '\u04ff' for c in token)
    marked = cyrillic or any(c in token.lower() for c in 'ąćęłńóśźżčďěňřšťůýž')
    return normalize(token), lead, tail, cyrillic, marked

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', None, 0)
    _, word, previous, slavic = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text, lead, tail, cyrillic, marked = spelling(token)
    slavic = min(100, slavic + 15) if marked else max(0, slavic - 1)
    cluster, weaker = text.rfind('stv'), text.rfind('sv')
    value, trigger = 0.0, None

    if cluster >= 0 and (cyrillic or slavic):
        before = len(text[:cluster].strip())
        after = len(text) - cluster - 3
        prefix_discount = 1.40 if before == 1 else 5.13 if before >= 2 else 0
        value = 9.46 - prefix_discount
        if after:
            value -= 3.78 if after == 1 else 4.68 if after == 2 else 4.26
        value -= 1.70 if not cyrillic else 0
        trigger = ('stv', before, after)
    elif lead and word.endswith('t') and lead.startswith('v'):
        value = 2.99 if cyrillic else 6.07 - (5.27 if not slavic else 0)
        value += 0.85 if word.endswith('st') else 0
        value -= 1.05 if len(lead) >= 3 else 0
        trigger = ('cross', 0, len(lead)-1)
    elif weaker >= 0 and cyrillic:
        after = len(text) - weaker - 2
        value = 2.44 - 0.93 * min(3, after)
        trigger = ('sv', 0, after)
    elif lead and word.endswith('s') and lead.startswith('v') and cyrillic:
        value = 1.88
        trigger = ('cross_sv', 0, len(lead)-1)
    elif lead and previous and word:
        kind, before, after = previous
        if after == 0:
            inherited = {'stv':4.24, 'cross':2.11, 'sv':0.97, 'cross_sv':2.39}
            value = inherited[kind]
            value += 3.24 if lead.startswith('ен') else 0
            value -= 1.70 if before >= 2 else 0
            value -= 2.36 if len(lead) >= 3 else 0
            value -= 0.12 if lead.startswith(('уе','ую','ова','ующ','уй')) else 0
        elif after == 1:
            value = 0.12
    elif cyrillic and 'tv' in text:
        value = 0.19
    elif cyrillic and 'v' in text and 'st' in text:
        value = 0.37

    value = max(0.0, value)
    if token in (' в', ' В'):
        value = -0.45
    word = word + lead if lead and lead == tail else tail
    if not tail:
        word, trigger = '', None
    return (doc, word[-40:], trigger, slavic), value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection unit 3984: the Slavic "stv" consonant cluster.

What it responds to: the letters s-t-v / с-т-в, spelled "ств" in Russian and
Ukrainian ("ство", "ства", "ствен-", "еств-", "обществ", "качеств"), and
"stw" / "stv" in Polish, Czech, Slovak and Estonian ("stwo", "stva", "stvo").
It fires on the token that carries the cluster, and also on a token that
completes it across a token boundary ("przedsiębiorst|wa", "Estest|vo",
"śledzt|wo", "ст|вовать"). Tokens right after a cluster inside the same
word ("ответств|енность", "лекарств|енного") get a weaker response.
Two dot-leader tokens ("····") carry a small constant value.

Causal: it reads only the current token and the text before it in the same
document, which it keeps in a carry (the last few characters).
"""
import re

READS = ()

CLUSTER = re.compile(r"ств|stv|stw")   # the letter cluster, lowercased
ONSET = re.compile(r"[vwв]")           # the letter that completes "st" + v/w
HIT = 5.0          # the cluster lies in this token, or is completed by it
AFTER = 2.0        # a word continuation right after a cluster
DOTS = 1.0         # run of middle dots


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev, prev_doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", doc)
    if prev_doc != doc:
        prev = ""  # a new document starts a new word
    if tok and set(tok) == {"·"}:
        value = DOTS
    elif CLUSTER.search(tok) or (prev.endswith(("st", "zt", "ст")) and ONSET.match(tok)):
        value = HIT
    elif CLUSTER.search(prev[-4:]) and tok[:1].isalpha():
        value = AFTER
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return ((prev + tok)[-6:], doc), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3985 — a near-silent component whose only clear effect is on
the first token of each document.

What the component does, as far as a simple description goes:
  * It is almost never important: its causal importance is ~0 everywhere, and switching
    it off barely changes the model's predictions.
  * Its activation is small and noisy (typical size ~0.04) at almost every token, with
    no concept that predicts the sign or size of that noise.
  * The one large, systematic effect is at the first token of a document (the start of
    a packed row, or the first token after <|endoftext|>), where the activation is
    typically around -0.15 to -0.2, but its sign depends on the token.

This program predicts that first-token effect from the kind of token it is, and predicts
0 everywhere else. The values are rough averages over a few thousand training rows.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation at a document's first token, by token type.
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = {
    "special": -0.22,  # chat/markup specials such as <|im_start|>
    "digit": -0.15,  # a number, e.g. "1", "23"
    "word": -0.17,  # a word with no leading space, e.g. "The", "ing"
    "other": -0.06,  # punctuation, space-prefixed words, code, etc.
}


def token_type(text: str) -> str:
    """A coarse, human-readable type for a token decoded alone."""
    if text.startswith("<|"):
        return "special"
    if text[:1].isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if text[:1].isalpha() and not text.startswith(" "):
        return "word"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's activation at the last token of the prefix."""
    first_token = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if not first_token:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE[token_type(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""A small approximation of several strong local text responses.

The main cue is a lowercase word fragment following an uppercase run:
for example IT + ext, where the word's initial T joined the preceding I.
An underscore joined to a capital initial is a related boundary cue.
There are also separate responses to 'wait', repeated middle dots,
NUL padding, and a context-free document separator. Most text gets zero.
These surface rules capture only part of the component's behavior.
"""
import re

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    position = 0 if first else carry[2] + 1
    value = 0.0

    if re.fullmatch(r'[a-z]{2,}', token):
        if re.search(r'[A-Z]{2,}$', previous):
            value = 0.35
        elif re.search(r'_[A-Z]$', previous):
            value = 0.40

    if token.strip().lower() == 'wait':
        value = 0.29
    if len(token) >= 2 and set(token) == {'·'}:
        value = -0.75
    if token == '\x00':
        value = -0.11 if position == 1 else -0.19
    if first and token == '<|endoftext|>':
        value = 1.76

    return (document, token, position), value

"""Method-chain dots (negative).

The component goes negative on the token that continues a method or member chain in
source code: the `.`, `->` or `::` about to name the next method or field. Everything
not listed predicts 0.

- A dot right after a call's closing parens, or after a closing quote or square
  bracket: `getInstance().`, `parse(x)->`, `"abc".`, `names["x"].`. These are almost
  always code chains, and predict about -2.2.
- A dot after some other closing bracket, `foo(x).` or `(x)).`: scaled by how code-like
  the last 24 tokens are (see CODE_TOKEN), from 0 for prose to about -2.2 for dense code.
  In prose, `(2010).` or `(Fig. 4E).`, the prediction is about 0.
- A dot that opens a continuation line of a fluent chain (indentation, then `.build()`):
  about -1.2.
- `->` after a name (`$this->`): about -0.6. `::` after a name (`std::`): about -0.3.
- `.out` in `System.out`: about -1.3.

"Code-like" is the share of the last 24 tokens, in the same document, that contain code
punctuation (brackets, `;`, `=`, `<`, `>`, `->`, `::`, `_`) or a dot followed by a name.
"""

import re
from collections import deque

READS = ()

WINDOW = 24
CODE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[{}();=\[\]<>_]|->|::|\.[A-Za-z_]")
CLOSER_THEN_DOT = re.compile(r"(.*[)\]\"'}])(\.|->)")
STRONG_CLOSERS = ("()", '")', "')", '"]', "']")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    recent = deque(maxlen=WINDOW) if new_doc else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = "" if new_doc else prefix.token_strings[-2]
    recent.append(1.0 if CODE_TOKEN.search(token) else 0.0)
    code_share = sum(recent) / len(recent)

    value = 0.0
    closer = CLOSER_THEN_DOT.fullmatch(token)
    if closer and closer.group(1).endswith(STRONG_CLOSERS):
        value = -2.2
    elif closer:
        value = -min(2.2, max(0.0, (code_share - 0.15) * 5))
    elif token == " ." and prev.strip() == "" and prev != "":
        value = -1.2
    elif token == "->":
        value = -0.6
    elif token == "::":
        value = -0.3
    elif token == ".out":
        value = -1.3
    return recent, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3988: a "year is coming" detector.

This component is mostly silent. It goes negative on the token just before a
YEAR in a written date, and on a few other spots where a number is expected
next. The prediction is made on that token, reading only the text so far:

- A separator (space, comma, apostrophe or slash) right after "Month day"
  or "Month day," (e.g. "born March 21, |1976", "May 11th, |2014"): about -2.
- A separator right after "day Month" (e.g. "02 Sep |2014", "21 nov. |2021"):
  about -2.
- A month word right after a day number ("3 June", "27 July"): about -1.5.
- A slash after "dd/dd" (e.g. "04/04/|2012"): about -2.5.
- Java or C# import lines ("import org...;" or "using System;"), on the
  keyword: about -2. Python imports are left at 0.
- A space that follows a word, in a document that already has a
  double-spaced numeral ("the memory controller hub  126"): about -0.7.
  This is the patent-style reference numeral. The model's activation is
  about -0.9 when the next token is the second space, but the program cannot
  see the future, so it uses the document-level cue.
- A middle-dot token "··": +1.2. In the sample this occurs only inside one
  long run of middle dots; elsewhere it is not seen, so this rule is a guess
  about that run, not a general fact.

Everything else is 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

MONTH = (
    r"\b(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September"
    r"|October|November|December|Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sept?"
    r"|Oct|Nov|Dec|déc)\.?"
)
# "March 21," / "March 21 " before a year
MONTH_DAY = re.compile(MONTH + r"[ \xa0]\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?[ ]?,?$", re.I)
# "21 March," / "21 March " before a year
DAY_MONTH = re.compile(r"\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?[ \xa0]" + MONTH + r",?$", re.I)
DOUBLE_SPACE_NUMERAL = re.compile(r"[a-z]  \d")
SEPARATORS = ("", ",", "'", "’", "/")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[prefix.position]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = (text[: -len(token)] if token else text)[-30:]
    word = token.strip()
    if word in SEPARATORS and MONTH_DAY.search(before):
        return None, -2.0
    if word in SEPARATORS and DAY_MONTH.search(before):
        return None, -2.0
    if token == " " and re.search(r"[a-z]$", before):
        if DOUBLE_SPACE_NUMERAL.search(text):
            return None, -0.7
    if word == "/" and re.search(r"\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}$", before):
        return None, -2.5
    if word in ("import", "using") and re.search(r";\n+$", before):
        return None, -2.0
    if word == "··":
        return None, 1.2
    if re.fullmatch(MONTH, word, re.I) and re.search(r"\d$", before):
        return None, -1.5
    return None, 0.0

Task words are modulated by nearby mathematical notation, sample/practice
modifiers, capitalization, and line position. Dots and parentheses closing

    'question': -0.158,
    'exercise': -0.038,
    'example': 0.158,
    'practice': 0.052,
    'paper': 0.088,
    'level': 0.08,
    'puzzle': -0.011,
    'answer': -0.092,

         'puzzle', 'paper'}

    r'(?i)\\(?:frac|sqrt|begin|sum|int|theta)\b|\$[a-z\\]|'
    r'\b(?:equation|algebra|geometry|trigonometry|arithmetic|fraction|'
    r'integer|polynomial|triangle|theorem|probability|derivative|matrix|'
    r'vector|slope|quadratic|math|mathematical)s?\b|'
    r'(?<!\w)[a-z]\s*[=+^]|\d\s*[-+*/=]\s*(?:\d|[a-z])')

    r'(?i)\b(?:sample|practice|worked|word|math|mathematical|challenge|'
    r'homework|test|similar|daily|aptitude|exam|example)\s+(?:\w+\s+)?$')

    r'(?i)\b(question|problem|exercise|example|test|quiz|q|que|ex|case|chapter|'
    r'section|figure|table|no|number)'
    r'\.?\s*[0-9]*$')

               ':', ':\n', ':\n\n'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 0, 0, 0)
    _, line, tail, age, position, items = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    stem = lower[:-1] if lower.endswith('s') else lower

    if stem == 'practise':
        stem = 'practice'
    if stem == 'solution':
        stem = 'answer'

    value = -0.003 + BASE.get(stem, 0.0)

        value += -0.285 * (not line.strip(' #*'))
        value += 0.119 * (not token[0].isspace())
        value += -0.231 * bool(MATH.search(tail))
        value += -1.255 * bool(MODIFIER.search(before))
    if stem in ('problem', 'question'):

    if lower == 'problems':
        value += 0.106
    if stem == 'level':
        value += -0.772 * word[0].isupper()
    if stem == 'example':
        value += -0.049 * bool(re.search(r'(?i)\bfor\s*$', tail))

                value += -0.276 * (position < 4)
                value += -0.382 * ('\n' in token)
                value += -0.073 * ('#' in line)

            elif punct == ')' and numeric:
                value += -0.137 + -0.064 * min(items, 3)
            elif punct == ')':
                value += -0.34
            elif punct == ':' and not numeric and position < 4:

            if punct in '.)':

    tail = (tail + token)[-800:]

"""Exercise-wording detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3994.

What it does: this component goes negative on the words that name a problem, question,
exercise, quiz or example, in any language, when they appear in maths or exam-style text
(solving problems, numbered questions). It is strongest when the surrounding text is dense
with digits, and it also goes negative on the exercise number that follows a label such
as "Q1", "Question 2" or "Example 3". Everywhere else it sits near zero, which is what
the rule predicts.

The prediction is a hand-set linear rule with weights fitted by least squares on training
rows:
  - English problem/question words: -0.49, plus -1.7 times the digit density of the last
    64 tokens (so -0.5 in prose, about -2 in dense maths),
  - foreign problem/question words (题, 問題, вопрос, ejercicio, ...): -0.2, plus -0.36 times
    the digit density,
  - the label words themselves (Q, Example, Quiz, Option, ...): about -0.05,
  - a number right after a label word: -0.34.
Digit density is counted within the current document only, as the model's attention is.
"""

READS = ()

PROBLEM_WORDS = {"problem", "problems", "question", "questions", "problema", "problemas"}
LABEL_WORDS = {"q", "q.", "example", "examples", "quiz", "option", "exercise", "exercises", "exam"}
FOREIGN_WORDS = ("题", "題", "問題", "问题", "вопрос", "задач", "ejercicio", "ercicio",
                 "exercicio", "pregunta", "문제", "problème", "exercice", "Aufgabe", "soal", "masala")
WINDOW = 64


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "digits": [], "prev": ""}
    word = token.strip().lower()
    dens = sum(carry["digits"]) / len(carry["digits"]) if carry["digits"] else 0.0
    if word in PROBLEM_WORDS:
        value = -0.49 - 1.69 * dens
    elif any(w in token for w in FOREIGN_WORDS):
        value = -0.20 - 0.36 * dens
    elif word in LABEL_WORDS:
        value = -0.05
    elif token.strip().isdigit() and carry["prev"] in LABEL_WORDS:
        value = -0.34
    else:
        value = 0.0
    carry["digits"] = (carry["digits"] + [float(token.strip().isdigit())])[-WINDOW:]
    carry["prev"] = word
    return carry, value

    (情况 "situation", 结果 / 結果 "result", 成果 "achievement", 效果 "effect",
    績 "record", 果 "fruit/result", 如何 "how", 不同 "different", 实际 "actual", ...).
    About -1.5 each.
  * Mildly positive: a few single kanji/hanzi and short words (分, 作, 返, 率, 結,
    負, 問題, ...), about +1.
  Every other token gets 0. The rest of the component's variance is a diffuse
  background over many tokens that no short rule captures.
"""

READS = ()

SHADDA = "ّ"
SHADDA_VALUE = 8.5

RESULT_WORDS = {
    "情况", "情況", "况", "況", "状况", "狀況", "情形", "具体情况", "实际情况", "实际",
    "的情况", "的情形", "结果", "結果", "的结果", "成果", "研究成果", "效果", "的效果",
    "績", "果", "如何", "不同", "的不同", "的情况",
}
RESULT_VALUE = -1.5

MILD_WORDS = {
    "分", "作", "作品", "返", "率", "結", "負", "問題", "表現", "演出", "不足", "細", "適用",
}
MILD_VALUE = 1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the last token of the prefix (depends only on that token)."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == SHADDA:
        return carry, SHADDA_VALUE
    if token in RESULT_WORDS:
        return carry, RESULT_VALUE
    if token in MILD_WORDS:
        return carry, MILD_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4002 (a diffuse, mostly token-driven feature).

What the component does, as far as a short program can say:
  * Its activation is small and noisy almost everywhere (sd about 0.04), and no
    concept we tried (token class, script, LaTeX, previous token, document genre)
    explains the sign or size of that noise.
  * Its large activations happen at the first token of a document (the token right
    after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row). There the activation depends
    only on the token itself (attention sees nothing else), and its sign varies
    from token to token, so this program predicts only the average size.
  * A run of repeated middle dots (U+00B7 "··", as in leader fill) gave a steady
    large activation of about 0.83 in the sample.

The program: 0.83 on a middle-dot token, a small positive value at the first token
of each document, and 0 elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

DOT_LEADER = "··"
DOC_START_VALUE = 0.08
DOT_VALUE = 0.83


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if token == DOT_LEADER:
        return carry, DOT_VALUE
    if starts_document:
        return carry, DOC_START_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Slavic "raz- / ras- / roz-" prefix syllables (Russian/Ukrainian/Polish "dis-, apart, re-").

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4004 reads a word as it is typed token by token. It fires on
the token that completes the syllable раз, рас or роз (or the Latin spellings raz, ras, roz)
at the start of a word, e.g. "раз" in "разрешение", "роз" in "розница", "рас" in "растение".
It also fires on a compound's second root that starts with that syllable after a linking "о",
e.g. "водораз" in "водоразделе", "многораз" in "многоразовый". Because a word can arrive split
across tokens, the program tracks the letters of the current word in `carry`; the syllable counts
when the current token finishes it (so "р" + "азв" fires on "азв", as in "Развитие").

Strength: the bare syllable "раз" / "роз" / "roz" is strongest (about 12, 16 when capitalised),
"рас" / "raz" / "ras" weaker (about 8 or 6), and a longer piece that merely starts with the syllable
("различ", "распростран") is weak (2). Everything else is 0.
"""

READS = ()

# syllable -> activation when the current piece is exactly this syllable
SYLLABLES = {"раз": 12.0, "роз": 12.0, "рас": 8.0, "raz": 8.0, "roz": 10.0, "ras": 6.0}
LINKING_VOWEL = "о"  # compound linking vowel, as in водо-раз-дел


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_document = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    # the word so far, from the carry; a new document or a token starting with a space starts a word
    before = "" if (new_document or token[:1].isspace()) else (carry or "")
    piece = token.strip()
    word = before + piece.lower() if piece.isalpha() else ""  # punctuation ends the word
    value = 0.0
    for syllable, strength in SYLLABLES.items():
        for start in range(len(word)):
            if not word.startswith(syllable, start) or start + len(syllable) <= len(before):
                continue  # the syllable must end inside the current token
            if start > 0 and word[start - 1] != LINKING_VOWEL:
                continue  # inside a word, only after a linking vowel
            if len(piece) > 3:
                strength = 2.0  # a longer piece that just starts with the syllable is weak
            elif piece[:1].isupper():
                strength *= 1.3
            value = max(value, strength)
    return word, value


def main():
    """Example: the tokens of "в результате водораздела" with their predictions."""
    words = ["в", " результате", " водор", "аз", "дел", "а"]
    carry = None
    for i, token in enumerate(words):
        prefix = type("P", (), {})()
        prefix.token_ids = list(range(i + 1))
        prefix.document_ids = [0] * (i + 1)
        prefix.token_strings = words[: i + 1]
        carry, value = step(carry, prefix, {})
        print(f"{token!r:16} {value:5.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 4005: a backslash detector whose sign depends on the text.

It fires on tokens that contain a backslash. Its size and sign depend on what kind of text the
backslash sits in, judged from the text just before it in the same document:

- A doubled backslash (`\\`, two characters: the usual spelling of a LaTeX line break, and of an
  escaped backslash in code) in LaTeX math (after a LaTeX command such as `\\frac`, `\\left`,
  `\\begin{...}`, `\\text`, `\\hline`, `\\nonumber`) is strongly negative, about -20.
- The same doubled backslash in code or escaped text (a `\\"` quote escape, a `\\name` path or
  namespace, a regex, `print("...\\n")`) is strongly positive, about +13.
- A doubled backslash with neither cue is positive, about +10.
- A single backslash is weakly positive: about +0.7 in LaTeX, +0.3 otherwise.

Everything without a backslash predicts 0. It is causal: it reads only earlier tokens and
resets at each document boundary.
"""
import re

READS = ()

LATEX = re.compile(
    r"\\(frac|dfrac|left|right|text|mathrm|mathbf|cdot|sqrt|alpha|beta|hfill|color|lim|sum|int"
    r"|over|vec|quad|ldots|begin|end|bmatrix|pmatrix|cases|overline|partial|rightarrow|Delta"
    r"|sigma|theta|nonumber|atop|dots|equiv|bmod|label|dagger|hat|rho|mu|mathcal|mathbb"
    r"|displaystyle|tau|omega|epsilon|lambda|chi|phi|eta|xi|pi|sim|le|ge|neq|approx|infty"
    r"|times|prime|bar|tilde|rm|bf|ref|eqref|cite|hline|mathop|operatorname|limits|big|Big"
    r"|bigl|bigr|mid|qquad)\b"
)
CODE = re.compile(r'\\"|\\\\[A-Za-z]')
WINDOW = 300


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    recent, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        recent = ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if "\\" in tok:
        before = recent[-200:]
        latex = LATEX.search(before) is not None
        if max(len(r) for r in re.findall(r"\\+", tok)) == 1:
            value = 0.7 if latex else 0.3
        elif latex:
            value = -20.0
        else:
            value = 13.0 if CODE.search(before) else 10.0
    recent = (recent + tok)[-WINDOW:]
    return (recent, doc), value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4006 -- a "the word GO" detector.

What it does: it fires on tokens that spell the English verb "go" in its forms
(go, going, goes, went, gone), and more weakly on "go" pieces inside other tokens
(".go" / "-go" / "/go" file or path pieces, and word fragments such as "ego",
"undergo", "outgoing", "Tango", "bingo"). It is silent on everything else.

Strength, from a 3000-row training sample and the harvest:
  went / gone  ~7   (strongest)
  goes         ~5.7
  go / going   ~5   in prose; about half that right after a blank token (code indentation),
                    and a little more after a subject such as "they", "you", "not", "to"
  ".go" / "-go" / "/go"  ~2-3.4
  other "go" fragments   ~3.5

Apart from that context tweak for "go", the activation is a function of the current
token alone. A lookup of each token's mean activation would explain about 0.72 of the
variance; this word rule explains about 0.57 and reads as plain English.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Whole words: the forms of "go" (any case, with or without a leading space).
WORD_VALUES = {"went": 7.4, "gone": 7.1, "goes": 5.7, "go": 5.0, "going": 5.0}

# "go" glued to punctuation, as in file extensions and paths.
PUNCT_GO = {".go": 2.1, "-go": 3.4, "/go": 2.9}

# Word pieces that carry the "go" spelling of "go" (ego, undergo, Tango ...).
GO_FRAGMENTS = {
    "ego", "gon", "ngo", "ango", "agon", "igo", "ingo", "gos", "goo", "gor",
    "tango", "bingo", "undergo", "undergoing", "undergone", "outgoing",
    "foregoing", "ongoing", "mango", "argo", "gol",
}
FRAGMENT_VALUE = 3.5

# Context for the "go" words: a blank token before (code indentation) weakens them,
# a subject before them strengthens them.
AFTER_BLANK = 0.5
AFTER_SUBJECT = 1.2
SUBJECTS = {"not", "they", "you", "to", "can", "could", "we", "i", "will", "and"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip().lower()
    if text in WORD_VALUES:
        value = WORD_VALUES[text]
        same_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
        if same_doc:
            before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
            if before.strip() == "":
                value *= AFTER_BLANK
            elif before.strip().lower() in SUBJECTS:
                value *= AFTER_SUBJECT
        return carry, value
    if text in PUNCT_GO:
        return carry, PUNCT_GO[text]
    letters = re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", text)
    if letters in GO_FRAGMENTS:
        return carry, FRAGMENT_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate journalistic attribution: quotes, sources, and reporting clauses.

Opening quotations are strongest at sentence boundaries, especially near a
reporting verb or named source.  `said`, other inflected reporting verbs, and
`that` following them receive smaller attribution signals.  Recent quotation
marks, capitalized names and official titles supply context, not token IDs.
First-person and passive `said` are weak; official sources strengthen it.
The short running summaries reset at document boundaries.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
REPORTING = set('''say tell add note state report explain announce claim warn
reply ask remark recall admit insist comment mention confirm declare reveal
assert acknowledge argue suggest reiterate contend concede testify opine
clarify confess estimate believe'''.split())
# Broader mentions of communication are useful as context, even uninflected.
CONTEXT_REPORTING = REPORTING | {'write', 'indicate', 'suggest'}
TITLES = set('''mr mrs dr president minister spokesman spokeswoman professor
director chairman official governor'''.split())
SOURCES = TITLES | {'police', 'authority', 'government', 'statement'}
BE_FORMS = {'is', 'was', 'be', 'been', 'being', 'are', 'were'}
SENTENCE_WORDS = set('''I We The A An It He She They This That There But And If
In On For To As At So You My His Her Our Their'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def word_classes(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) if word.isascii() and word.isalpha() else set()
    inflected = any(b in REPORTING and b != word
                    for b in wordnet.base_forms(word, 'verb')) if word.isalpha() else False
    return (bool((forms | {word}) & CONTEXT_REPORTING),
            'tell' in forms or word == 'tell', inflected)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry['doc'] != doc or '<|endoftext|>' in token:
        carry = dict(doc=doc, tail='', report=0., quote=0., names=0.,
                     code=0., inflected=False, boundary=False)
    s = carry
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    reporting, telling, inflected = word_classes(token)
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', s['tail'])
    last = words[-1] if words else ''
    name = last[:1].isupper() and last not in SENTENCE_WORDS
    third_person = last.lower() in {'he', 'she'}
    sentence_end = bool(re.search(r'[.!?][\s”"’]*$', s['tail']))
    opening = (word.startswith(('“', '«', '„', '‘', '"'))
               and not any(q in word[1:] for q in ('"', '”', '»')))
    curly = opening and word[0] != '"'
    capital_quote = opening and len(word) > 1 and (
        word[1].isupper() or word[1] == '(')

    value = .001
    if opening:
        if not sentence_end:
            value = .08 if s['report'] < .7 else (
                3.3 if s['boundary'] else .74)
        elif not curly:
            value = .66 if s['names'] < .5 else (
                1.9 if s['report'] < .15 else 5.9)
        elif capital_quote or s['report'] >= .05:
            value = 5.8
        else:
            value = 4.2 if s['quote'] < .05 else 1.2
    elif lower == 'said':
        if last == 'I' or last.lower() in BE_FORMS:
            value = -.1
        elif set(wordnet.base_forms(last, 'noun')) & SOURCES:
            value = 4.0
        elif name:
            value = 1.3 if s['quote'] < .05 and s['names'] < 2 else 5.0
        else:
            value = 3.7 if third_person else .83
    elif telling:
        value = 2.5 if name else (.85 if s['names'] >= .5 else .005)
    elif lower == 'that' and s['inflected']:
        value = .12 if s['code'] >= .01 else (
            1.4 if s['quote'] >= .01 else .89)
    elif inflected:
        value = 1.4 if s['quote'] >= .35 or third_person else (
            .72 if name else .12)
    elif lower in TITLES:
        value = .78 if s['quote'] >= .01 else .27

    # Recency-weighted counts of recognizable linguistic cues.
    is_name = ((token.startswith((' ', '\n')) or not s['tail'])
               and word[:1].isupper() and word not in SENTENCE_WORDS
               and not sentence_end)
    s['names'] = .94 * s['names'] + is_name
    s['report'] = max(.9 * s['report'], float(reporting))
    closing = bool(re.search(r'[”»]|[,!?]["“]', token))
    s['quote'] = max(.9 * s['quote'], float(opening or closing))
    s['code'] = .9 * s['code'] + .1 * bool(re.search(r'[{}=\\;`]|</', token))
    s['boundary'] = bool(re.search(r'[.!?:。]([\s”"’]*)$', token))
    s['inflected'] = inflected
    s['tail'] = (s['tail'] + token)[-180:]
    return s, float(value)

"""Quotation-onset detector for news-style quotes (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4007).

What it does, in plain terms. This component switches on where a news story hands the
floor to a source:
  * the reporting verb that names the speaker: "Bhavnagri said", "he added", "Lunsford stated",
    or the Chinese/Spanish equivalents (表示, 告诉记者, dijo). A reporting verb after a name or
    pronoun is strong; a passive like "is said to" is not.
  * the opening quotation mark of a direct quote ( “ " ‘ « ), strongest when it follows a
    sentence break, colon or comma shortly after a reporting verb, and weaker when the story
    has already attributed speech earlier.
It stays near zero for quoted terms and scare quotes, fiction dialogue, legal definitions,
and ordinary text. Most of the variance is in the diffuse small activations of ordinary text,
which this program does not model.
"""

READS = ()

SPEECH_WORDS = frozenset(
    "said says say added adds told tells stated noted notes explained explains asked replied "
    "wrote warned announced argued claimed insisted recalled remarked observed confirmed "
    "admitted declared suggested opined indicated praised spoke described believes "
    "dijo señaló afirmó manifestó indicó explicó añadió déclaré sagte".split()
)
# Chinese reporting verbs, matched inside a token (告诉记者 = "told reporters").
SPEECH_CJK = ("表示", "告诉", "说道", "称", "指出", "补充", "透露", "强调", "介绍")
# Words before which a verb like "said" is passive or infinitival, not a speaker tag.
AUX_WORDS = frozenset(
    "to be is was were been by will can could would should may might must not and or the a an "
    "it that this which what how with being are am".split()
)
OPEN_QUOTES = frozenset("“‘«「„")
NEAR = 20  # tokens since a reporting verb that still count as "this story is quoting people"

# Typical activation (fit to data) for each situation.
SPEECH_FIRST, SPEECH_LATER = 0.6, 1.7
QUOTE_NEAR_PUNCT, QUOTE_NEAR_BARE = 3.7, 1.1
QUOTE_LATER_PUNCT, QUOTE_LATER_BARE = 2.5, 0.2
QUOTE_PLAIN_PUNCT, QUOTE_PLAIN_BARE = 0.5, 0.1
AFTER_SPEECH = 0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, tokens since last reporting verb, reporting verbs so far, straight quotes so far)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 10**6, 0, 0)
    _, since, count, straight = carry

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    lead = tok.lstrip()[:1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    prev_word = before.strip().lower()
    after_break = before.strip()[-1:] in (".", ":", ",") or "\n" in before

    # Straight quotes alternate open/close within a document; curly ones are unambiguous.
    if lead == '"':
        is_open = straight % 2 == 0
        straight += 1
    else:
        is_open = lead in OPEN_QUOTES

    is_speech = (word in SPEECH_WORDS and prev_word not in AUX_WORDS) or any(
        c in tok for c in SPEECH_CJK
    )
    value = 0.0
    if is_speech:
        value = SPEECH_LATER if count > 0 else SPEECH_FIRST
        count += 1
    elif is_open:
        if since <= NEAR:
            value = QUOTE_NEAR_PUNCT if after_break else QUOTE_NEAR_BARE
        elif count > 0:
            value = QUOTE_LATER_PUNCT if after_break else QUOTE_LATER_BARE
        else:
            value = QUOTE_PLAIN_PUNCT if after_break else QUOTE_PLAIN_BARE
    elif prev_word in SPEECH_WORDS:
        value = AFTER_SPEECH

    since = 0 if is_speech else since + 1
    return (doc, since, count, straight), value

"""Layer-1 MLP unit 4008 (down_proj column). Its activation is almost exactly that unit's
value. It reads the text each token adds to the decoded prefix, so a character split
across byte tokens counts once its last byte arrives. It fires on words for testing and
experience, danger and risk, possibility and necessity, and insurance, and dips on formal
project, period and approval nouns. Everything else is predicted as 0."""

READS = ()

# a single character the token completes (matched only when it is the whole addition)
CHARS = {
    "験": 6.4, "険": 6.0, "險": 4.7, "险": 5.0,  # experience / test; danger
    "検": 3.6, "驗": 2.8, "验": 1.8, "험": 3.5,  # inspection / test; test (Korean)
    "講": 1.6, "讲": 1.0,                       # lecture
    "項": -1.1,                                 # item
}

# words the token adds (matched as substrings of the addition)
WORDS = [
    (("必要",), 3.0),
    (("可能", "可能性"), 3.0),
    (("保险", "保險"), 2.5),
    (("危险", "危險"), 1.7),
    (("也许", "也許", "或许"), 1.4),
    (("重要",), 1.2),
    (("风险", "風險"), 1.0),
    (("필요", "가능", "중요"), 2.5),
    (("项目", "項目"), -2.5),
    (("期间", "期間", "期限", "假期", "假日", "审批", "采集", "资金", "利益", "事项"), -1.0),
]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    now = prefix.text_prefixes[t]
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[t - 1] if t > 0 else ""
    i = 0
    while i < min(len(now), len(before)) and now[i] == before[i]:
        i += 1
    added = now[i:]
    if added in CHARS:
        return None, CHARS[added]
    for keys, value in WORDS:
        if any(key in added for key in keys):
            return None, value
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4010 — a document-start detector.

The component writes a large signal into the residual stream on the first token of each
document (and at the first token of a packed row), and is near zero everywhere else.
Its size depends on that first token's look:

- If the first token is a mid-sentence word (a leading space followed by letters, such as
  " the", " a", " to", " of", " it"), the document is starting in the middle of a sentence
  and the component fires strongly (about 32).
- Otherwise (a capitalised word, a digit, punctuation, a newline, or a bare space) it fires
  weakly (about 12).
- Every other token predicts 0.

Document starts are found from document ids: a token starts a document if it is the first
position of the row or its document id differs from the previous token's.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return None, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    mid_sentence = token[:1] == " " and token[1:2].isalpha()
    return None, 32.0 if mid_sentence else 12.0

"""A few strong text-boundary responses, with near-zero background.

At a document opening, distinguish source-code declarations and comment styles.
Within text, recognize number-ending dots (not list numbers or second decimal
points), traceback-like line labels, C++ std:: and GitHub domain notation.
Also respond to question/challenge headings and reasoning/tool markup.
A leading run of carriage returns and paired middle dots are positive triggers.
Constants summarize observed training responses. These rules cover selected
cases, not all token-specific variation.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Document-opening constructs; spacing is significant to the tokenizer.
OPENING = {
    'class': 1.537,
    ' class': 1.329,
    'def': 0.504,
    'const': -1.618,
    'var': -1.053,
    'using': -0.571,
    'package': -0.214,
    'import': 0.181,
    '#include': 0.191,
    '#ifndef': -0.820,
    '<?': -0.447,
    '/*': -0.963,
    '//': -0.769,
    '//\n': 2.548,
    'Question': 0.433,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        position, previous, tail, only_returns = 0, '', '', True
    else:
        _, position, previous, tail, only_returns = carry

        value = OPENING.get(token, value)

        value = 2.338

        value = 0.489
    elif token == '<?' and position > 0:
        value = -0.08
    elif previous == '<?' and token == 'php':
        value = 1.211 if position == 1 else 0.31
    elif token == '.':
        number = re.search(r'\d+$', tail)

            before = tail[:number.start()]

                value = -0.06

                value = -0.04 if digits == 2 else 0.0
            else:
                value = {1: 0.146, 2: 0.08, 3: 0.05}.get(digits, 0.01)
    elif token == ':' and position == 1 and previous == 'Question':

The unit is negative on the words that deal with a problem or an obstacle: verbs of
avoiding, handling, facing, overcoming or enduring it (avoid, prevent, handle, face,
navigate, withstand, resist ...), the prepositions that open its object (against,
under, despite), the determiner right after such a verb (solve the), and the preposition
after a word that names a hazard or a response to one (subject to, susceptible to, rid
of, free of, deal with, comply with). It is also negative on "any" and "no" after
"without" (strongly) or after "with", "are", "has", "have" (less so). It is mildly
positive on the word "problem" and on words about what happens to things (typically,
happen, affect, vary).
"""

tackle tackling meet meeting mitigate against under despite counter cope coping combat
respond responding resolve resolving address addressing solve solving withstand navigate
tolerate survive endure relieve resist heal dealing oppose

решить преодолеть избежать предотвратить""".split())

satisfy detect fix correct cover however otherwise respect potential met eliminate treat
addressed resolved managed handled prevented avoided""".split())

consequences impact effects presence aware solution solutions response responses reply answer""".split())

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()

    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""

- the chat tag '</think>' itself: about -0.15;
