"""A spelling-E signal, not a topic detector.

Short pieces with an early E (especially their first vowel) get a large value.
Case, transliteration, and dictionary frequency refine this. Recent word
frequencies estimate the surrounding language so English grammatical uses can
be distinguished from foreign word fragments. A little signal carries into
another piece of the same word. Digit-following E and end-of-text markers have
separate adjustments. This deliberately omits arbitrary token-specific offsets.
"""
import math
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = 'en de fr es pt it nl pl cs tr sv da nb fi ro hu vi id'.split()
PRONOUNS = set('''i you he she it we they me him her us them my your his its
our their mine yours hers ours theirs myself yourself himself herself itself
ourselves yourselves themselves'''.split())
DEICTIC = set('the this that these those there here where when then'.split())
AUXILIARIES = set('''am is are was were be been being have has had do does did
can could shall should will would may might must'''.split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = PRONOUNS | DEICTIC | AUXILIARIES | set('''a an of for to in on
at by with as from and or but if than while'''.split())
SUFFIXES = {'ed', 'es', 'er', 'ers', 'est', 'en'}


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(s):
    raw = s.strip()
    letters = ''.join(c for c in raw if c.isalpha())
    names = [unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in letters]
    latin = bool(letters) and all('LATIN' in name for name in names)
    cyrillic = any('CYRILLIC' in name for name in names)
    greek = any('GREEK' in name for name in names)
    han = any('CJK' in name for name in names)
    kana = any('HIRAGANA' in name or 'KATAKANA' in name for name in names)
    t = anyascii(letters).lower()
    n, p = len(t), t.find('e')
    strength = math.exp(-0.15 * max(n - 3, 0)) if 0 <= p < 5 else 0.0
    value = 0.002 + 0.212 * greek
    if strength:
        first_vowel = not any(c in 'aiouy' for c in t[:p])
        weight = (0.570, 0.705, 0.578, 0.394, 0.330)[p]
        weight += (0.570, 0.237, 0.148, 0.224, 0.221)[p] * first_vowel
        weight += 0.280 * letters.isupper() - 0.254 * (not s[0].isspace())
        weight += (-0.180 * cyrillic + 0.314 * greek
                   - 0.329 * han + 0.144 * kana)
        value += strength * weight
    value += 0.211 * (p >= 0 and n == 1)
    value -= 0.003 * (p >= 0 and t.count('e') > 1)
    frequencies = tuple(zipf_frequency(letters.lower(), lang)
                        for lang in LANGUAGES) if latin else (0.0,) * 18
    evidence = bool(latin and len(raw) >= 2 and raw.isalpha()
                    and s[0].isspace())
    return value, strength, frequencies, evidence, raw.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        scores, previous_e, ends_letter, ends_digit = [0.0] * 18, 0.0, False, False
    else:
        _, scores, previous_e, ends_letter, ends_digit = carry
    language = max(range(18), key=scores.__getitem__)
    value, strength, frequencies, evidence, word = spelling(s)
    continues = bool(s and s[0].isalpha() and ends_letter)
    whole = bool(s and (s[0].isspace() or s[0] in '\"\'([{'))
    if strength:
        frequency = frequencies[language] if s[0].isspace() else 0.0
        weight = (-0.278 * max(frequency - 4, 0)
                  + 0.041 * max(frequency - 5, 0)
                  + 0.091 * max(frequency - 6, 0))
        if language == 0 and whole:
            weight -= 0.184 * (word in PRONOUNS)
            weight += 0.034 * (word in DEICTIC)
            weight -= 0.088 * (word in AUXILIARIES)
        weight -= 0.025 * continues
        weight -= 0.273 * (continues and word in SUFFIXES)
        value += strength * weight
    if continues:
        value += previous_e * (0.109 if strength else 0.424)
    value += 0.060 * previous_e * (word in FUNCTION_WORDS)
    value += 0.539 * (word == 'e' and ends_digit)
    value += first * (0.128 - 0.261 * strength)
    if s == '<|endoftext|>':
        value = 3.83 if first else value + 0.616
        scores = [0.0] * 18
    elif evidence:
        scores = [0.92 * old + 0.08 * new
                  for old, new in zip(scores, frequencies)]
    carry = (doc, scores, strength, bool(s and s[-1].isalpha()),
             bool(s and s[-1].isdigit()))
    return carry, float(value)

without an e. Two special cases: the end-of-text token fires strongly, and a
half-character replacement token (a fragment of a multi-byte character) fires weakly.

about a third of its variance on held-out text); these few rules capture most of that.

    "take its he she where when then these those".split()

    core = "".join(E_LOOKALIKE.get(ch, ch) for ch in s.strip().lower())
    if core == "e":  # the bare letter: a variable, exponent or symbol
        return None, 1.5 if s.strip() == "E" else 1.1
    if not core.isalpha():  # punctuation or code, e.g. "*e" or "(e"
        return None, 0.35 if "e" in core else 0.0
    if core in COMMON:
        return None, 0.0
    short = len(core) <= 3
    if "e" in core:
        if s.startswith(" "):  # a whole word that starts with a space
            return None, 0.6 if short else 0.2
        if not short:  # a long word piece
            return None, 0.3
        # a short word piece: the earlier the e, the stronger
        return None, (1.0, 0.7, 0.2)[min(core.index("e"), 2)]
    if not s.startswith(" ") and short:  # a short word piece with no e
        return None, 0.1
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate an end-of-piece 'e' feature, usually with negative activation.

Short Latin pieces ending in e or es respond most; capitals and word-internal
pieces respond more. Listed grammatical words and common derivational suffixes
respond less. Transliteration extends the rule to kana, Greek and Cyrillic.
Small script and punctuation biases cover some of the remaining activity.
This is a spelling-class approximation, not a per-token activation table.
"""
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()
GRAMMATICAL_WORDS = set('''
he she we me ye thee thou mine thine be are were have
 the some same where
'''.split())
FRENCH_GERMAN_FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
de le les des que qui une un der die das eine jede je ne ce du
'''.split())
DERIVATIONAL_SUFFIXES = set('able ible ive ative tive ize ate'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def spelling(text):
    value = 0.015
    parts = regex.findall(r'\p{L}+', text)
    word = parts[-1] if parts and text.endswith(parts[-1]) else ''
    ending, short, grammatical = False, False, False
    if word and regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Latin}+', word):
        plain = ''.join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', word)
                        if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower()
        plural = plain.endswith('es')
        ending = plain.endswith('e') or plural
        if ending:
            length = len(plain) - int(plural)
            short = length <= 3
            value += -0.75 + 0.05 * min(length, 12)
            value -= 0.16 * (not text.startswith(' '))
            value -= 0.26 * word.isupper() + 0.18 * word.istitle()
            value += 0.27 * plural
            grammatical = plain in GRAMMATICAL_WORDS
            foreign = plain in FRENCH_GERMAN_FUNCTION_WORDS
            value += 0.53 * grammatical + 0.26 * foreign
            grammatical = grammatical or foreign
            if grammatical:
                value += 0.10 * (word.istitle() + (not text.startswith(' ')))
            value += 0.57 * (plain in DERIVATIONAL_SUFFIXES)
    elif word and regex.fullmatch(
            r'[\p{Greek}\p{Cyrillic}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]+', word):
        value -= 0.47 * anyascii(word).lower().endswith('e')
    if regex.search(r'[^\p{Latin}\p{ASCII}\p{P}\p{S}\p{Z}\p{N}]', text):
        value -= 0.04
    value -= 0.28 * ('\ufffd' in text)
    value -= 0.50 * ('^' in text)
    value -= 0.18 * bool(regex.search(r'>|≤|≥|≠|→|←|⇒|⇐', text))
    value -= 0.66 * bool(regex.search(r'[•·]', text))
    value -= 0.13 * bool(regex.fullmatch(r'\s*[=.#`~]{3,}\s*', text))
    return value, ending, short, grammatical


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value, ending, short, grammatical = spelling(text)
    if (ending and not text.startswith(' ') and prefix.position > 0
            and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]
            and prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:].isalpha()):
        value -= 0.26 * short + 0.69 * grammatical
    return None, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4027 -- a "mid-word fragment" detector.

This component mostly sits near zero. It goes strongly negative on a token that is an
unfinished piece of a word, above all a piece ending in a silent "e" (ke, ze, ure, ice,
ime, one, NAME), and mildly negative on a whole word ending in "e" (crate, vice, Guide,
name, code). Such pieces are where the model still expects the word to continue.
The first token of each document is mildly positive.

The program reads only the newest token and whether a new document starts there.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Short common words ending in "e" that are whole words, not fragments: near zero.
FUNCTION_E = {"the", "be", "me", "he", "we", "are", "have", "here", "there", "where",
              "come", "give", "make", "take", "use", "see", "more", "some", "one",
              "three", "while", "since", "before", "after", "were", "she", "free"}


def syllables(word):
    """Rough syllable count: number of vowel groups."""
    return max(1, len(re.findall(r"[aeiouy]+", word)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    lower = word.lower()

    # First token of a document (the model's attention resets there): mildly positive.
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return None, 0.6

    if not word.isalpha():
        return None, 0.0

    caps = word.isupper() and len(word) > 1
    if tok[:1] != " ":
        # A word piece with no leading space: the word is unfinished.
        if lower.endswith("e"):
            return None, -1.4 if caps else -0.85   # silent-e fragment, e.g. "ke", "ure", "NAME"
        if lower.endswith("es"):
            return None, -0.5                      # plural-style fragment
        if lower[-1] in "éеыè":
            return None, -0.45                     # non-English vowel ending mid-word
        return None, 0.0

    # A whole word starting with a space: only the ones ending in "e" are negative.
    if lower.endswith("e") and lower not in FUNCTION_E:
        if caps:
            return None, -1.3
        return None, -0.6 if syllables(lower) <= 2 else -0.3
    return None, 0.0

"""Formulaic-phrase detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4028.

What the component does, in plain terms: it is quiet almost everywhere (its activation
is near zero at most tokens), and it fires on the word that completes a fixed phrase in a
few kinds of formulaic text. Positive: the "@@" hunk marker in a git diff, the "-" that
follows it, and "git" in "diff --git"; the words that finish patent and court boilerplate
("Court of", "COURT OF", "Regarding claim", "invention relates", "are rejected under");
and forum boilerplate ("Title:", "Author Message", "Created by", "email protected"). Weakly
negative inside URLs ("http://") and Java package names ("import com.", "import org.").

The program looks only at the current token and the one before it. Values are the mean
activations measured on training text, rounded.
"""
READS = ()

# (previous token, current token) -> activation; tokens are compared without surrounding spaces
PHRASES = {
    ("--", "git"): 1.1,        # diff --git
    ("@@", "-"): 1.3,          # the "-" after a hunk marker
    ("COURT", "OF"): 2.4,
    ("Court", "of"): 1.0,
    ("Regarding", "claim"): 1.8,
    ("invention", "relates"): 0.9,
    ("rejected", "under"): 0.8,
    ("are", "rejected"): 2.0,
    ("Title", ":"): 2.3,
    ("Author", "Message"): 1.5,
    ("Created", "by"): 0.6,
    ("email", "protected"): 0.9,
    ("", '"github'): 0.75,   # "github in a Go import, after indentation
    ("http", "://"): -0.26,
    ("import", "com"): -0.3,
    ("import", "org"): -0.2,
    ("DOCUMENT", "ATION"): -0.9,
    ("Last", "edited"): -0.8,
}
HUNK_MARK = 1.1  # any "@@" token, whatever precedes it

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if (prev, cur) in PHRASES:
        return None, PHRASES[(prev, cur)]
    if cur == "@@":
        return None, HUNK_MARK
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 4029 (v3): a weak 'international / world' word detector.

The component is almost always near zero and has rare, large negative responses. The
clearest ones are on the tokens 国际 and 世界 (international, world) and on the English
words World and International. This program predicts a small negative value on exactly
those tokens and 0 everywhere else; the magnitude is kept small because the same words
are not always negative.
"""

READS = ()

INTERNATIONAL_WORDS = {"国际", "世界", "国内", "World", "International"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    value = -1.0 if token in INTERNATIONAL_WORDS else 0.0
    return carry, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4030 — an exception-handling keyword detector.

The component fires strongly on the words that introduce exception handling in
source code: `throws` (Java method signatures), `catch`, `throw`, `raise`, `except`
(Python), and exception class names such as `Exception` and `IOException`. It also
fires weakly on `try` and `else` in code. The same words in ordinary English prose
("all sectors except agriculture", "a ball that throws") give about zero, so the
program first checks that the recent text looks like code (brackets, operators,
semicolons, or a line break).

A small negative response appears on the fragment " z" (and similar) inside Dutch
text, so the program predicts a negative value there. Dutch is detected from a few
common Dutch function words.

Activations are the predicted values in the component's native scale.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation of each keyword when it is used as code.
KEYWORDS = {
    "throws": 16.0, "throw": 5.0, "catch": 6.0, "raise": 6.0, "except": 4.0,
    "Exception": 3.0, "exception": 2.0, "IOException": 8.0, "try": 0.6,
    "else": 0.8,
}
CODE_MARKS = set("(){};=[]:")
DUTCH = set("de het een van en dat die niet zijn ik op voor met ook maar als bij naar".split())


def is_code(prefix, n=12):
    # Recent text contains code punctuation or a line break.
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-n:])
    return any(c in CODE_MARKS for c in recent) or "\n" in recent


def is_dutch(prefix, n=20):
    # At least two common Dutch function words in the recent text.
    words = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-n:]).lower().split()
    return sum(w in DUTCH for w in words) >= 2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip(" \t.")
    value = KEYWORDS.get(word, 0.0)
    if value and not is_code(prefix):
        value = 0.0
    if word == "z" and is_dutch(prefix):
        value = -4.0
    return carry, value

"""Job and occupation words: fires on the piece of text that names a job, post or vocation.

What it models: layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4031 is nearly silent on ordinary text and
fires strongly on the token that completes a word meaning "job / occupation / post":
  - the Chinese/Japanese character 職 or 职 (职业 occupation, 职务 post, 职称 job title,
    职工 employee, 兼职 part-time job, 職員 staff), and Korean 직 (직업, 직원);
    the staff character 員/员 after 職 and 원 after 직 also fire;
  - the English stems "occupational" and "vocational" / "vocation" (strong) and the
    bare word "occupation" (weaker); Spanish "vocación" as well.
Words that merely contain these letters, such as "invocation", do not count.
Everything else predicts 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

JOB_CHARS = "職职"                 # 職 / 职: job, post, duty
KOREAN_JOB = "직"                  # 직: as in 직업 (job) and 직원 (employee)
JOB_FOLLOWERS = ("員", "员", "工", "원")  # 職員 staff, 職工 worker, 직원 employee
STRONG = re.compile(r"\b(occupational|vocational|vocation|vocaci[oó]n)$", re.IGNORECASE)
WEAK = re.compile(r"\b(occupation|occupations|ocupaci[oó]n)$", re.IGNORECASE)
JOB_VALUE = 5.0
WORD_VALUE = 5.0
WEAK_VALUE = 1.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (recent text, document id, last token); reset at each new document.
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[1] != doc:
        recent, last = "", ""
    else:
        recent, last = carry[0], carry[2]
    text = (recent + tok)[-40:]
    carry = (text, doc, tok)

    if "单职业" in tok:                 # a game term ("single class"), not a job
        return carry, 0.0
    if any(c in JOB_CHARS for c in tok):
        return carry, JOB_VALUE
    if tok.strip().startswith(KOREAN_JOB):
        return carry, JOB_VALUE
    if tok.strip() in JOB_FOLLOWERS and any(c in JOB_CHARS + KOREAN_JOB for c in last):
        return carry, JOB_VALUE
    if STRONG.search(text):
        return carry, WORD_VALUE
    if WEAK.search(text):
        return carry, WEAK_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0
